content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Marietta

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-leadership experience, or a high school diploma plus five years of equivalent experience. Review PMI's formal education and work-hour requirements to confirm you meet the baseline. Eligibility verification happens before you apply.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. You'll attend synchronous sessions from any location, learning core project management frameworks, practices, and exam strategy directly from active certified practitioners. This formal instruction satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After finishing coursework, submit your PMP application to PMI through their official portal. You'll report your education, project experience, and training completion. Once PMI approves your application, you'll receive authorization to schedule your exam and pay the associated examination fee.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—study guides, practice tests, and instructor feedback—to reinforce your learning. Schedule your proctored exam through PMI's testing partner. On exam day, you'll answer 180 multiple-choice questions in a timed, computer-based format.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: The PMP is valid for three years. Maintain it by earning Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, volunteer work, or professional activities. Before your three-year cycle ends, renew your credential with PMI to remain current and recognized across Marietta's aerospace, defense, healthcare, and government sectors.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.
